topics.name: Descriptive Statistics Explorer
topics.concept: An interactive statistics workbench that computes means, medians, modes, quartiles, variance, and skewness for synthetic health-measurement datasets. It renders histograms and box plots as ASCII art and explains what each statistic reveals about the distribution shape. All datasets are generated on the fly for teaching.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG draws samples from normal, skewed, and bimodal distributions with health-like scales.
topics.real_world_use: Used in biostatistics courses as a first hands-on statistics lab.

topics.name: Confidence Interval Lab
topics.concept: A teaching simulator that repeatedly samples from a known synthetic population, builds confidence intervals for the mean, and shows what fraction capture the true value. Learners can change the confidence level and sample size to see intervals widen or narrow. It makes the meaning of coverage concrete.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG samples from a synthetic population with a known true mean for repeated experiments.
topics.real_world_use: Used in statistics education to build intuition for interval estimation.

topics.name: Hypothesis Test Workbench
topics.concept: A guided workbench that runs t-tests, chi-square tests, and proportion tests on synthetic datasets, reporting test statistics, p-values, and plain-language interpretations. It checks assumptions like normality and expected cell counts before running each test. Every dataset is invented for the demo.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates two-group and contingency-table data with controllable effect sizes.
topics.real_world_use: Used in biostatistics training for practicing test selection and interpretation.

topics.name: Clinical Sample Size Calculator
topics.concept: A study-design calculator that computes required sample sizes for comparing two means or two proportions given power, significance level, and a minimum detectable effect. It shows how the required size grows as the effect shrinks. The math is standard power-analysis formulas implemented from scratch.
topics.data_idea: No synthetic data is needed; the tool computes sizes directly from the input parameters.
topics.real_world_use: Used by researchers planning trials and surveys to justify enrollment targets.

topics.name: Statistical Power Curve Plotter
topics.concept: A visualization tool that draws power curves showing how the chance of detecting an effect rises with sample size for several effect sizes. It helps learners see why underpowered studies miss real effects. Curves are computed from the normal approximation implemented in pure Python.
topics.data_idea: Curves are computed analytically from the input parameters with no sampling needed.
topics.real_world_use: Used in study-design courses to teach the sample-size, effect, and power tradeoff.

topics.name: Survival Curve Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A Kaplan-Meier teaching tool that builds survival curves from synthetic time-to-event data with censoring, comparing two groups with a log-rank style test computed from scratch. It reports median survival per group and shades confidence bands. All event times are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG draws event times from exponential distributions with group-specific hazards plus censoring.
topics.real_world_use: Used in clinical biostatistics courses to teach survival analysis concepts.

topics.name: Dose-Response Curve Fitter (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A curve-fitting demo that fits a four-parameter logistic model to synthetic dose-response data using a from-scratch gradient descent. It estimates the EC50 and Hill slope and reports goodness of fit. Data is invented for pharmacology teaching, not real compound data.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates responses from a true logistic curve with Gaussian noise.
topics.real_world_use: Used in pharmacology education to teach dose-response modeling.

topics.name: Bland-Altman Agreement Analyzer
topics.concept: A method-comparison tool for synthetic paired measurements from two devices that plots differences against means, computes bias and limits of agreement, and flags proportional bias with a regression of difference on mean. It teaches when two measurement methods agree well enough.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates paired readings with controllable bias and random error.
topics.real_world_use: Used in clinical measurement courses to teach agreement analysis.

topics.name: ROC Curve Builder (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A diagnostic-accuracy demo that sweeps a decision threshold over synthetic test scores for diseased and healthy groups, tracing sensitivity against one-minus-specificity. It computes the area under the curve with the trapezoid rule and marks the threshold maximizing Youden's index. All scores are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG draws test scores from overlapping distributions for the two groups.
topics.real_world_use: Used in diagnostic-test education to teach ROC analysis.

topics.name: Predictive Value Prevalence Adjuster
topics.concept: A Bayes-rule calculator that converts a test's sensitivity and specificity into positive and negative predictive values across a range of disease prevalence values. It shows why the same test performs differently in screening versus referral populations. Computation is pure arithmetic.
topics.data_idea: Values are computed directly from the input parameters with no sampling.
topics.real_world_use: Used in epidemiology teaching to explain predictive values.

topics.name: Incidence Rate Tracker (Synthetic)
topics.concept: An epidemiology counter that computes incidence rates and person-time denominators from synthetic cohort follow-up records. It compares rates across exposure groups with rate ratios and confidence intervals. All cohorts are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates follow-up records with exposure-dependent event hazards.
topics.real_world_use: Used in epidemiology courses to practice rate calculations.

topics.name: Odds Ratio Calculator
topics.concept: A two-by-two table analyzer for synthetic case-control data that computes odds ratios with confidence intervals and runs a chi-square test of association. It handles zero cells with a small continuity correction and explains the interpretation. Tables are invented for teaching.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG fills two-by-two tables with a controllable true odds ratio.
topics.real_world_use: Used in epidemiology training for association measures.

topics.name: Relative Risk Simulator
topics.concept: A cohort-study simulator that follows synthetic exposed and unexposed groups, counts outcomes, and computes relative risk with confidence intervals. Learners can dial the true risk up or down and watch estimates converge with larger cohorts. All subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG assigns outcomes with group-specific probabilities.
topics.real_world_use: Used in epidemiology courses to teach cohort-study analysis.

topics.name: Confounding Demonstration Lab
topics.concept: A teaching lab that generates synthetic data where a crude association reverses or disappears after stratifying by a confounder, demonstrating Simpson's paradox. It computes crude and stratum-specific estimates side by side. The paradox is constructed deliberately for the lesson.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds strata with opposing within-stratum and pooled associations.
topics.real_world_use: Used in epidemiology education to make confounding unforgettable.

topics.name: Trial Randomization Checker
topics.concept: A randomization simulator that assigns synthetic trial participants to arms by simple, block, or stratified randomization and then checks baseline balance across arms. It shows how blocking keeps arm sizes equal over time. Participants are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG assigns arms and generates baseline covariates per participant.
topics.real_world_use: Used in clinical-trial training to teach randomization methods.

topics.name: Adverse Event Tabulator (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A safety-table builder that tabulates synthetic adverse events by treatment arm, computing event rates, risk differences, and flagging events with notable imbalances. It produces a formatted safety summary table. All events are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates adverse events with arm-specific rate multipliers.
topics.real_world_use: Used in trial-reporting training for safety tables.

topics.name: Missing Data Pattern Explorer
topics.concept: A teaching tool that injects missingness into a complete synthetic dataset under MCAR, MAR, and MNAR mechanisms and compares complete-case, mean-imputation, and multiple-imputation style estimates. It shows how the mechanism biases results. Data is invented for the lesson.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds a complete dataset then deletes values per the chosen mechanism.
topics.real_world_use: Used in biostatistics courses to teach missing-data concepts.

topics.name: Multiple Testing Correction Demo
topics.concept: A false-discovery lab that runs many hypothesis tests on synthetic null data, counts the false positives, and then applies Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg corrections to show the difference. It makes the multiple-comparisons problem tangible. All data is null by construction.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates test statistics, mostly null with a few true signals.
topics.real_world_use: Used in genomics-adjacent statistics teaching for FDR concepts.

topics.name: Bootstrap Resampling Lab
topics.concept: A resampling teacher that estimates the sampling distribution of a statistic by bootstrapping a synthetic dataset thousands of times, building percentile confidence intervals. It compares bootstrap intervals against the theoretical ones. The method is implemented from scratch.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates a skewed synthetic dataset where theory and bootstrap differ instructively.
topics.real_world_use: Used in statistics education to teach resampling inference.

topics.name: Permutation Test Demo
topics.concept: An exact-inference demo that tests a group difference by shuffling synthetic group labels thousands of times to build the null distribution. It compares the permutation p-value with the t-test p-value. Labels are fictional and the data invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates two groups with a controllable true difference.
topics.real_world_use: Used in statistics courses to teach randomization-based inference.

topics.name: Linear Model Fitter (Health Data)
topics.concept: A from-scratch ordinary least squares fitter on synthetic health predictors that reports coefficients, standard errors, R-squared, and residual diagnostics. It detects multicollinearity with variance inflation factors and plots residuals as ASCII. Data is invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds predictors with correlations and a known true model.
topics.real_world_use: Used in regression courses as a transparent OLS implementation.

topics.name: Logistic Regression Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A binary-outcome modeler that fits logistic regression by gradient descent on synthetic data, reporting odds ratios, predicted probabilities, and a confusion matrix at a chosen threshold. It demonstrates how linear predictors map to probabilities. All data is fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates predictors and binary outcomes from a true logistic model.
topics.real_world_use: Used in biostatistics teaching for binary-outcome modeling.

topics.name: Poisson Count Model Demo
topics.concept: A count-data modeler that fits Poisson regression from scratch on synthetic event counts like clinic visits per month, reporting rate ratios and checking for overdispersion. It compares Poisson and quasi-Poisson style standard errors. Counts are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG draws counts from Poisson and negative-binomial generators.
topics.real_world_use: Used in health-services research training for count outcomes.

topics.name: ANOVA Workbench (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A group-comparison workbench that runs one-way ANOVA on synthetic multi-group measurements, partitioning variance into between and within components with a from-scratch F test. It follows up with pairwise comparisons and Tukey-style adjustments. Groups are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates group measurements with controllable mean differences.
topics.real_world_use: Used in experimental-design courses to teach ANOVA.

topics.name: Nonparametric Test Lab
topics.concept: A rank-based test collection implementing Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and Kruskal-Wallis from scratch on synthetic skewed data where t-tests misbehave. It compares parametric and nonparametric p-values side by side. Data is invented for the lesson.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG draws skewed samples where rank tests shine.
topics.real_world_use: Used in biostatistics courses for nonparametric methods.

topics.name: Correlation Explorer
topics.concept: A correlation playground computing Pearson and Spearman coefficients on synthetic variable pairs with scatter plots in ASCII, including Anscombe-style datasets where correlation misleads. It warns when outliers drive the result. All data is invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates pairs with linear, nonlinear, and outlier-contaminated patterns.
topics.real_world_use: Used in introductory statistics to teach correlation pitfalls.

topics.name: Regression to the Mean Demo
topics.concept: A teaching simulator showing how extreme first measurements drift toward the average on retest, using synthetic paired readings with imperfect correlation. It explains why naive before-after comparisons overstate treatment effects. Readings are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates paired readings with a set test-retest correlation.
topics.real_world_use: Used in methods courses to teach a classic bias.

topics.name: Screening Test Metrics Lab
topics.concept: A metrics workbench computing sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios from synthetic screening results against a known disease status. It shows how metrics shift with threshold and prevalence. All subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates test scores and true disease statuses.
topics.real_world_use: Used in clinical epidemiology teaching for test metrics.

topics.name: Likelihood Ratio Nomogram (Digital)
topics.concept: A digital Fagan-style nomogram that converts pre-test probability through a likelihood ratio into post-test probability with an animated probability bar. It teaches Bayesian updating for diagnostic reasoning. Computation is pure arithmetic on inputs.
topics.data_idea: Values are computed directly from the input parameters.
topics.real_world_use: Used in evidence-based medicine teaching for Bayesian diagnosis.

topics.name: Meta-Analysis Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A teaching meta-analysis that pools synthetic study estimates with fixed-effect and random-effects models computed from scratch, drawing a forest plot in ASCII. It quantifies heterogeneity with I-squared and shows funnel-plot asymmetry. Studies are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates study estimates around a true effect with heterogeneity.
topics.real_world_use: Used in systematic-review courses to teach evidence synthesis.

topics.name: Publication Bias Funnel Plot Checker
topics.concept: A bias-detection demo plotting synthetic study effects against precision and testing funnel asymmetry with a regression test implemented from scratch. It contrasts unbiased and suppressed-negative study sets. Studies are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates study sets with optional suppression of nonsignificant results.
topics.real_world_use: Used in meta-analysis training for publication-bias concepts.

topics.name: Crossover Trial Simulator
topics.concept: A within-subject trial simulator generating synthetic crossover data with period and carryover effects, analyzed with paired methods from scratch. It shows the efficiency gain over parallel designs and the danger of carryover. Subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates subject responses per period with carryover.
topics.real_world_use: Used in trial-design courses to teach crossover methodology.

topics.name: Cluster Trial Designer
topics.concept: A design tool for synthetic cluster-randomized trials that computes the design effect from intracluster correlation and adjusts sample-size needs. It simulates clustered outcomes to show why ignoring clustering underestimates variance. Clusters are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates correlated outcomes within clusters.
topics.real_world_use: Used in trial-design training for clustered designs.

topics.name: Equivalence Test Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A TOST teaching demo that tests whether a synthetic generic-versus-brand difference falls within an equivalence margin, rather than testing for any difference. It plots the confidence interval against the margin. Data is invented for the lesson.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates group measurements with a small true difference.
topics.real_world_use: Used in biostatistics courses to teach equivalence thinking.

topics.name: Non-Inferiority Calculator
topics.concept: A margin-based calculator for synthetic non-inferiority trials that checks whether the confidence interval for the treatment difference excludes the non-inferiority margin. It contrasts the conclusion with a superiority analysis of the same data. Inputs are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates arm outcomes around the assumed difference.
topics.real_world_use: Used in trial-design education for non-inferiority concepts.

topics.name: Interim Analysis Simulator
topics.concept: A group-sequential demo that simulates a synthetic trial with planned interim looks, applying alpha-spending boundaries computed from scratch. It shows how early stopping for efficacy or futility changes the operating characteristics. Data is invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG accumulates trial data look by look with the true effect.
topics.real_world_use: Used in advanced trial-design courses for sequential methods.

topics.name: Bayesian Updating Demo
topics.concept: A conjugate-prior teacher that updates beta-binomial beliefs about a synthetic event rate as data arrives, animating the posterior narrowing. It compares Bayesian credible intervals with frequentist ones on the same data. All data is invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates binary outcomes at the true rate.
topics.real_world_use: Used in biostatistics courses introducing Bayesian thinking.

topics.name: Propensity Score Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: An observational-study teaching tool that estimates propensity scores with a from-scratch logistic model on synthetic confounded data, then matches treated and control subjects and compares adjusted versus crude effects. Confounding is built in deliberately. Subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates covariates influencing both treatment and outcome.
topics.real_world_use: Used in causal-inference courses for propensity methods.

topics.name: Instrumental Variable Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A two-stage least squares teaching demo on synthetic data with a valid instrument, recovering a causal effect that naive regression gets wrong due to unmeasured confounding. It checks instrument strength with a first-stage F statistic. Data is invented for the lesson.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds instrument, treatment, and outcome with hidden confounding.

topics.name: Difference-in-Differences Demo
topics.concept: A policy-evaluation simulator generating synthetic outcomes for treated and control regions before and after an intervention, estimating the effect with the classic double difference. It tests the parallel-trends assumption visually. Regions are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates regional trends with a post-policy treated shift.
topics.real_world_use: Used in health-policy courses for quasi-experimental methods.

topics.name: Regression Discontinuity Demo
topics.concept: A cutoff-design teacher generating synthetic outcomes around an eligibility threshold with a true jump at the cutoff, estimated with local linear regression from scratch. It shows bandwidth sensitivity of the estimate. Data is invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG draws running variables and outcomes with a discontinuity.
topics.real_world_use: Used in causal-inference teaching for discontinuity designs.

topics.name: Growth Mixture Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A longitudinal teaching tool that fits a from-scratch mixture model to synthetic repeated measures, discovering latent trajectory classes like improvers and decliners. It assigns class probabilities per subject. Subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates trajectories from class-specific growth curves.
topics.real_world_use: Used in longitudinal-data courses for mixture concepts.

topics.name: Item Response Theory Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A Rasch-model teaching demo estimating item difficulties and person abilities from synthetic test responses with from-scratch joint maximum likelihood. It plots item characteristic curves as ASCII. Items and persons are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates responses from true item and person parameters.

topics.name: Questionnaire Reliability Calculator
topics.concept: A scale-reliability tool computing Cronbach's alpha and item-total correlations from synthetic questionnaire responses, flagging items that drag reliability down. It demonstrates how scale length affects alpha. Responses are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates responses with a controllable true reliability.
topics.real_world_use: Used in health-measurement courses for reliability analysis.

topics.name: Factor Analysis Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: An exploratory factor analysis teaching tool running from-scratch principal-axis factoring on synthetic correlated survey items, with varimax-style rotation and scree plots in ASCII. It recovers planted factor structures. Items are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates item responses from planted factor loadings.

topics.name: Disease Seasonality Decomposer (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A time-series teaching tool decomposing synthetic weekly case counts into trend, seasonal, and residual components with a from-scratch moving-average method. It estimates peak week and seasonal amplitude. Counts are invented for epidemiology teaching.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds case counts from trend plus seasonal waves plus noise.

topics.name: Epidemic Curve Plotter (Synthetic)
topics.concept: An outbreak-curve builder that bins synthetic symptom-onset dates into an epidemic curve, estimates the reproduction number from the growth phase, and overlays a fitted curve. All cases are fictional training data.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates onset dates from a branching-process style growth.
topics.real_world_use: Used in field-epidemiology training for epi curves.

topics.name: Vaccine Efficacy Calculator (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A trial-analysis demo computing vaccine efficacy from synthetic vaccinated and unvaccinated case counts with confidence intervals, plus number needed to vaccinate. It shows efficacy under different attack rates. Data is invented for teaching.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG assigns cases with arm-specific risks.
topics.real_world_use: Used in vaccinology education for efficacy concepts.

topics.name: Attributable Risk Lab
topics.concept: A population-impact workbench computing attributable risk and population attributable fraction from synthetic exposure-outcome data under different exposure prevalences. It translates fractions into preventable-case counts for a fictional population. Data is invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates exposure and outcome statuses.
topics.real_world_use: Used in epidemiology courses for population-impact measures.

topics.name: Rate Standardization Demo
topics.concept: A direct-standardization teacher that adjusts synthetic crude rates for differing age structures using a standard population, showing how rankings flip after adjustment. It computes standardized rate ratios with confidence intervals. Populations are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates age-specific rates and population structures.
topics.real_world_use: Used in epidemiology teaching for confounding by age.

topics.name: Life Table Builder (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A demography tool building abridged life tables from synthetic age-specific mortality rates, computing life expectancy and survival probabilities column by column. It compares two fictional populations side by side. Rates are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates age-specific rates with Gompertz-like growth.
topics.real_world_use: Used in demography and public-health teaching.

topics.name: QALY Calculator Demo (Educational)
topics.concept: A health-economics teaching calculator that combines synthetic survival times with utility weights to estimate quality-adjusted life years for two fictional interventions. It computes incremental cost-effectiveness ratios from demo costs. Labeled educational with invented numbers.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates survival and utility trajectories per arm.
topics.real_world_use: Used in health-economics courses for cost-effectiveness concepts.

topics.name: Markov Health-State Model Demo
topics.concept: A cohort simulation moving a synthetic population through health states with transition probabilities, accumulating costs and QALYs over cycles. It runs probabilistic sensitivity analysis by resampling inputs. States and numbers are fictional teaching constructs.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG drives state transitions per the input probability matrix.

topics.name: Decision Tree Analyzer (Health Economics)
topics.concept: An expected-value calculator for a synthetic clinical decision tree with chance nodes, payoffs, and probabilities entered by the learner. It rolls back the tree, computes expected values per strategy, and runs one-way sensitivity analysis. The tree is a teaching example.
topics.data_idea: Probabilities and payoffs are learner inputs; sensitivity sweeps vary them systematically.

topics.name: Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis Runner
topics.concept: A Monte Carlo engine that resamples synthetic model inputs from distributions and records the resulting cost-effectiveness outcomes, drawing cost-effectiveness acceptability curves as ASCII. It quantifies decision uncertainty. Inputs are fictional teaching distributions.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG draws parameter sets and evaluates the demo model each iteration.
topics.real_world_use: Used in health-economics courses for uncertainty analysis.

topics.name: Value of Information Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A teaching calculator estimating the expected value of perfect information for a synthetic decision model by comparing decide-now versus decide-after-learning outcomes. It ranks parameters by their contribution to decision uncertainty. All numbers are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG samples parameters and evaluates outcomes per draw.

topics.name: Disease Cluster Detector Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A spatial-scan teaching tool that slides circular windows over a synthetic map of case and population counts, computing likelihood ratios to flag the most unusual cluster. It adjusts for multiple testing with Monte Carlo p-values. Geography is fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG places cases with an injected hotspot for detection.
topics.real_world_use: Used in spatial-epidemiology teaching for cluster detection.

topics.name: Syndromic Surveillance Simulator
topics.concept: An aberration-detection simulator streaming synthetic daily symptom counts with injected outbreak signals, running CUSUM-style detectors from scratch and scoring detection timeliness. It compares detector sensitivity settings. Counts are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG streams baseline counts with outbreak-shaped injections.

topics.name: Contact Tracing Model (Educational)
topics.concept: A network teaching model where synthetic cases have contacts, and tracing with configurable coverage and speed reduces onward transmission in the simulation. It estimates the tracing effort needed to bend the curve. People and networks are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds contact networks and simulates tracing and transmission.
topics.real_world_use: Used in infectious-disease courses for tracing concepts.

topics.name: Herd Immunity Visualizer
topics.concept: An SIR teaching simulator sweeping vaccination coverage to show when synthetic outbreaks fizzle versus explode, with animated compartment curves. It derives the critical coverage from the reproduction number. Populations are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG initializes compartments and steps the SIR difference equations.
topics.real_world_use: Used in epidemiology education for herd-immunity intuition.

topics.name: Testing Threshold Tuner (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A decision-threshold optimizer for a synthetic diagnostic score that balances the costs of false positives and false negatives to find the cost-minimizing cutoff. It sweeps thresholds and plots total expected cost. Scores and costs are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates scores with overlapping diseased and healthy distributions.

topics.name: Risk Model Calibration Plot Builder
topics.concept: A calibration checker binning synthetic predicted risks against observed event rates, drawing calibration curves with confidence bands and computing calibration slope and intercept. It contrasts well-calibrated and miscalibrated demo models. Data is invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates predictions and outcomes with controllable miscalibration.
topics.real_world_use: Used in prediction-model courses for calibration concepts.

topics.name: Decision Curve Analysis Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A net-benefit teaching tool computing decision curves for synthetic risk models across threshold probabilities, comparing treat-all, treat-none, and model-guided strategies. It is implemented from scratch on invented data. Labeled educational.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates risks and outcomes for the compared models.

topics.name: Number Needed to Treat Calculator
topics.concept: A treatment-impact translator converting synthetic trial event rates into absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction, and number needed to treat with confidence intervals. It shows how NNT changes with baseline risk. Data is invented for teaching.
topics.data_idea: Event counts are derived from the input rates with a synthetic sample size.

topics.name: Fragility Index Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A robustness checker that flips synthetic trial outcomes one at a time to find how many flips change the significance verdict, demonstrating trial fragility. It reports the fragility index and quotient. Trials are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates trial tables near the significance boundary.
topics.real_world_use: Used in critical-appraisal teaching for result robustness.

topics.name: Treatment Heterogeneity Explorer
topics.concept: A subgroup-analysis teaching tool that estimates synthetic treatment effects across subgroups and tests for interaction from scratch, warning about the perils of unplanned subgroup fishing. Subgroups are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates outcomes with optional true subgroup interactions.

topics.name: Survey Weighting Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A survey-adjustment teacher applying synthetic sampling weights and post-stratification to a biased fictional sample, showing estimates move toward the known population truth. It computes design effects from the weights. Data is invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG draws a biased sample from a known synthetic population.
topics.real_world_use: Used in survey-methods courses for weighting concepts.

topics.name: Capture-Recapture Estimator Demo
topics.concept: A population-size teaching tool applying the Lincoln-Petersen estimator to synthetic two-sample capture histories, with Chapman bias correction and confidence intervals. It shows sensitivity to the closed-population assumption. Animals are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG simulates captures from a known fictional population.
topics.real_world_use: Used in wildlife-epidemiology teaching for population estimation.

topics.name: Age-Period-Cohort Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: An identification-problem teacher generating synthetic rates with known age, period, and cohort effects and showing why the three cannot be separated without constraints. It fits constrained models from scratch. Rates are invented.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds rates from planted age, period, and cohort components.

topics.name: Competing Risks Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A cumulative-incidence teacher contrasting Kaplan-Meier with competing-risks estimates on synthetic data where a competing event precludes the event of interest. It computes cumulative incidence functions from scratch. Subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates times with two competing event types.
topics.real_world_use: Used in survival-analysis courses for competing risks.

topics.name: Recurrent Events Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A repeated-events teaching tool modeling synthetic gap times between recurrent episodes with frailty terms from scratch, showing how ignoring within-subject correlation biases variance. Subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates correlated gap times per subject.

topics.name: Joint Longitudinal-Survival Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A joint-modeling teacher linking synthetic biomarker trajectories to event times in one from-scratch model, showing efficiency gains over separate analyses. It is a simplified teaching implementation. Subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates linked biomarker and event-time data.

topics.name: Causal Diagram Quiz
topics.concept: A DAG-based quiz engine presenting synthetic causal diagrams and asking learners to identify confounders, mediators, colliders, and valid adjustment sets, with explanations for each answer. Diagrams are generated for teaching.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG assembles DAGs with planted confounding, mediation, and collider structures.
topics.real_world_use: Used in causal-inference courses for DAG literacy.

topics.name: Mediation Analysis Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A path-analysis teacher decomposing a synthetic total effect into direct and indirect paths through a mediator with from-scratch regressions and bootstrap confidence intervals for the indirect effect. Data is invented for the lesson.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds exposure, mediator, and outcome with planted paths.
topics.real_world_use: Used in methods courses for mediation concepts.

topics.name: G-Formula Demo (Synthetic)
topics.concept: A standardization teaching tool estimating a synthetic causal effect by modeling the outcome and averaging predictions under each treatment level, contrasting with the crude estimate under confounding. Subjects are fictional.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates confounded treatment assignment and outcomes.
topics.real_world_use: Used in causal-inference teaching for standardization.

topics.name: Target Trial Emulation Demo (Synthetic)
